text:
maria-ml: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection PR (merged ~2h ago) I'm seeing a ~7% drop in average batch utilization on p64 pools. Not huge but consistent across 3 hosts. Anyone else noticing changes in the queue shaping/formation? :thinking:
jonathan-runtime: I saw it too. Queue depth spiked for short windows and token/sec for tail requests dropped. Might be the new heuristic picking smaller batch cutoffs for short-context requests.
ryan-sre: CI perf alert rolled in: perf-bot flagged a regression for the continuous batcher metric `batch_util_pct` on p64-west-1 at 16:12 UTC. Matching time with the deploy.
perf-bot: [automated] regression_detected: metric=batch_util_pct, p64-west-1, delta=-6.8%, p=0.003, window=15m
elaine-telemetry: I pulled profiles from two affected instances. KV cache hit-rate stayed flat, but the microbatch formation histogram shifted left — median batch size went from 8 -> 5 for <128 token requests.
maria-ml: That aligns with hypothesis: the kernel selector change aimed to favor lower-latency paths which may favor smaller microbatches. Can we confirm which code path changed the batching cutoff?
jonathan-runtime: It was in pr #4122 — changed `BatchCutoffEstimator` to include `kernel_pref` bias. Patch: 
```py
if kernel_pref == 'low-latency':
    cutoff = max(2, int(0.6 * expected_batch))
```
So it intentionally reduces cutoff when low-latency kernel chosen.
ryan-sre: Quick mitigation idea: revert kernel bias or add an adaptive check that keeps batch size floor at 6 for p64 pools. Reverting might be risky for tail latency.
elaine-telemetry: We can gate by token-budget target. Telemetry shows token/sec for 99th worsened by ~12ms/ token but p50 improved ~3ms. If we want overall throughput we should maintain batch size floor.
maria-ml: Agreed — tradeoff between p50 and utilization. Proposal: temporary rollout that disables kernel_bias for dedicated p64 pools and we monitor `batch_util_pct`, `queue_depth`, `tokens_per_sec`.
jonathan-runtime: I'll open a rollback-flag PR with a config flag `runtime.disable_kernel_bias_for_p64=true` and a canary rollout for 10% of p64 capacity.
perf-bot: [automated] action_suggested: add config-flag + canary, monitor metrics for 30m, alert on batch_util_pct delta > -3%
elaine-telemetry: I'll add dashboards: 1) rolling 5m batch_util_pct by pool, 2) microbatch_size histogram, 3) token/sec per host. Will also add a quick SQL to compute median batch size shift: 
```sql
SELECT pool, quantile(0.5)(batch_size) FROM batching_events WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY pool;
```
maria-ml: Thanks — timeline? Want to avoid customer impact. If we can have the flag and canary up in 30m we can decide next steps after 30m of metrics.
jonathan-runtime: Working on PR now, should be ready for review in ~20m. Ryan can trigger canary deploy once merged.
ryan-sre: Copy. I'll stand by for rollback if anything spikes.
maria-ml: Cool. One follow-up: please attach perf profiles (flamegraphs) for both paths so we can quantify CPU delta vs utilization. Also add any KV cache effects.
elaine-telemetry: Will do — planning to attach artifacts to the PR. I'll also post lightweight alert if microbatch median <6 for p64. :eyes:
